mcqs.q: From 2008-2019 in BC SPCA shelters, which relinquishment reasons rose in proportion over time?
mcqs.e: "Too many" (OR 1.16) and "behavior" (OR 1.34) increased, while financial problems declined (OR 0.94).

mcqs.q: What was the single most commonly reported primary reason for dog relinquishment?
mcqs.e: "Too many dogs" at 19% was the top reported reason, ahead of housing (17%).

mcqs.q: The authors highlight improving pet-inclusive housing as an intervention especially for which setting?
mcqs.e: Housing-issue surrenders were predicted in larger centers, so pet-inclusive housing was flagged for large population centers.

mcqs.q: Which CIMD factor predicted increased odds of surrendering pit bull-labeled dogs in both study areas?
mcqs.e: Situational Vulnerability predicted higher odds of pit bull-labeled dog surrender in both Metro Vancouver and Kamloops.

mcqs.q: In Metro Vancouver, increased owner-surrender risk for multiple owner-related reasons was predicted by which factor (versus Residential Instability in Kamloops)?
mcqs.e: Ethnocultural Composition drove owner-related surrenders in Vancouver, whereas Residential Instability did so in Kamloops.

mcqs.q: What does the study conclude about provision of animal services for vulnerable groups?
o: It may need to be location-specific
It has no effect on retention
mcqs.e: Differing predictors across areas suggest services like veterinary care should be tailored by location.

mcqs.q: For puppies and kittens, how did the outgoing (adoption) community's Situational Vulnerability compare to the incoming (surrender) community's?
mcqs.e: Median outgoing SV quintiles were significantly lower, supporting flow of animals from more to less vulnerable communities.

mcqs.q: How many of the four CIMD dimensions differed significantly between surrendering and adopting communities?
mcqs.e: Three dimensions differed (Ethnocultural Composition, Situational Vulnerability, Economic Dependency); Residential Instability did not.

mcqs.q: The authors argue animal sheltering is best considered from which framework?
mcqs.e: The data are presented as further support for a One Welfare perspective on sheltering.

authors: Li, Gordon, Idle, Hui, Chan, Seguin, Delwart

mcqs.q: Which agent did viral metagenomics implicate as most likely responsible for the shelter vomiting outbreak?
mcqs.e: Feline astrovirus was present in all pools at high prevalence and temporally tied to the outbreak.

mcqs.q: What did testing of asymptomatic control cats housed in the same areas reveal?
mcqs.e: 5 of 9 (56%) clinically unaffected control cats also shed astrovirus, indicating significant asymptomatic shedding.

mcqs.q: Fecal samples collected ~1 year before and after the outbreak supported which conclusion?
o: Astrovirus is a normal commensal in this shelter
Astrovirus was only temporarily associated with the outbreak
The outbreak was caused by panleukopenia
mcqs.e: No astrovirus was detected before or after, so the virus was temporarily linked to the outbreak rather than commensal.

journal: Journal of Feline Medicine and Surgery

mcqs.q: Which factor carried roughly a 13-fold increased risk of death in underage nursery kittens?
mcqs.e: Panleukopenia diagnosis (and being in the lightest weight group) conferred ~13x greater mortality risk.

mcqs.q: Upper respiratory infection (URI) was associated with approximately what increase in mortality risk?
mcqs.e: URI was associated with almost a four-fold increased risk of death.

mcqs.q: The identified pre-mortem signs are intended to support which shelter decisions?
mcqs.e: The authors frame the prognostic indicators as aids for monitoring, intervention, and euthanasia decisions.

authors: Yoak, Haile, O'Quin, Belu, Birhane, Bekele, Murphy, Medley, Vincent, Steward, Shiferaw, Tafese, Garabed, Pieracci

mcqs.q: How did the median price owners were willing to pay compare with the actual cost of vaccination?
o: It was less than the actual cost
mcqs.e: Willingness-to-pay (median ~25 birr) was below the real cost, supporting the need for subsidized or free vaccine.

mcqs.q: What vaccination coverage threshold is cited as needed for canine rabies elimination?
mcqs.e: The 70% coverage threshold is the stated target for canine rabies elimination.

mcqs.q: Which delivery strategy did results support incorporating to maximize coverage?
mcqs.e: Many owners were unwilling to travel, so door-to-door vaccination combined with subsidies was endorsed.

authors: McCobb, Crawford, Harrold, Levy, Perkins, Reinhard, Watson

mcqs.q: How many themes did the meeting identify around shelter medicine program sustainability?
mcqs.e: Four themes emerged: external pressure, funder expectations, time horizons, and perceptions of shelters/veterinarians.

mcqs.q: Which was NOT one of the identified sustainability themes?
o: External pressure from leadership and stakeholders
mcqs.e: Vaccine supply was not a theme; the four were external pressure, funder expectations, time horizons, and perceptions.

mcqs.q: The discussion focused on sustaining shelter medicine in which context?
mcqs.e: The meeting addressed long-term success of shelter medicine curricula in academic training.

authors: Grijalva, Levy, Walden, Crawford, Pine, Hernandez
journal: Journal of Shelter Medicine and Community Animal Health

mcqs.q: What was the observed human:dog ratio among stray (free-roaming) dogs in Quito?
mcqs.e: Free-roaming dogs showed a 58:1 HD ratio, versus 3.5:1 for indoor-kept dogs.

mcqs.q: What was the prevalence of households with dogs infected with intestinal parasites?
mcqs.e: 28% of households (95% CI 21-37) had one or more dogs infected with intestinal parasites.

mcqs.q: Which intestinal parasite was most frequent in indoor-kept dogs?
mcqs.e: Ancylostoma spp. (zoonotic hookworm) was the most frequent parasite in dogs kept indoors.

authors: Alberigi, Campos, Branco, Bendas, Brum, Calixto, Alves, Pinheiro, Knackfuss, Labarthe, Levy, Mendes-de-Almeida

mcqs.q: What was the feline heartworm antigen seroprevalence among the 586 cats tested?
mcqs.e: Seroprevalence of heartworm antigen was 1.2% despite the high local canine prevalence.

mcqs.q: Which clinical findings were significantly associated with heartworm-positive cats?
mcqs.e: Heartworm-positive results were significantly associated with vomiting and abnormal lung sounds.

mcqs.q: Because treatment options for infected cats are limited, what do the authors emphasize?
mcqs.e: With limited treatment, prevention via prophylaxis and owner education is prioritized.

mcqs.q: What is the authors' main conclusion about applying a Ricker model to TNR programs?
o: It is inappropriate for assessing TNR effectiveness
It is the gold standard for TNR
It accurately predicts cat population stability
mcqs.e: The authors conclude the Ricker model is inappropriate for evaluating TNR effectiveness.

mcqs.q: Why does the Ricker model fail for free-roaming cat populations?
o: It predicts wild population swings inconsistent with observed stability
mcqs.e: The model predicts large population swings that don't match the relative stability of real free-roaming cat populations.

mcqs.q: Which alternative model do the authors favor for predicting needed sterilization effort?
o: A stochastic model accounting for cat movement in and out
mcqs.e: A stochastic model that accounts for immigration/emigration of cats is deemed better suited.

authors: Wandesforde-Smith, Levy, Lynn, Rand, Riley, Schaffner, Wolf

mcqs.q: Through what ethical lens does the paper frame management of cats living beyond domesticity?
mcqs.e: The article advances moral pluralism in managing human-cat-wildlife interactions.

mcqs.q: The central policy tension reviewed is between cat eradication advocates and proponents of what alternative?
mcqs.e: The conflict is between eradication advocates and supporters of TNR variants.

mcqs.q: What outcome do the authors warn this cat-wildlife conflict risks producing?
mcqs.e: They note the conflict raises the prospect of stalemate and seek ways to move beyond it.

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a reported benefit of triage and appointment-based shelter admission?
mcqs.e: Reported outcomes included reduced euthanasia, lower disease, and better morale; euthanasia decreased, not increased.

mcqs.q: Unmanaged, unscheduled admission frequently leads to what consequence?
o: Animal influx exceeding capacity, causing crowding and disease
mcqs.e: Unscheduled intake often pushes influx beyond capacity, producing crowding, stress, disease, and euthanasia.

mcqs.q: The article draws a parallel between shelter triage/appointment models and practices in which sector?
mcqs.e: Triage and appointment-based services are explicitly likened to those long used in human healthcare.
